name: AquaCarbon Safe Water
description: The purpose of this PoA is to disseminate low-GHG water purification technologies in Ghana, thereby reducing the need to boil water, which is generally done on unimproved stoves that use firewood and/or charcoal. With only 30% of the population having access to clean cooking fuels and technologies in Ghana,  the project addresses a critical challenge in sustainable water treatment and fuel consumption. The reduction in fossil fuel combustion will lead to a reduction in carbon emissions. The PoA is planned to have a geographical scope expansion in the future.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
methodology: GS Methodology for emission reductions from safe drinking water supply

name: Community-based Landscape Restoration in Zambia (COLAREZA)
description: World Vision Australia (WVA), World Vision Zambia (WVZ) and FORLIANCE intend to implement this Program of Activities with the objective to restore forest landscapes in several regions in Zambia making use of Assisted Natural Regeneration and other forest restoration and management methods. The POA seeks to create and enhance carbon sinks, reduce pressure on woody biomass, restore the local ecology and biodiversity and apply measures of climate smart agriculture whilst delivering significant socio-economic benefits to the local communities. The intent is to develop community-led revegetation projects using primarily Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) on degraded community land to ensure longterm social benefits and carbon removal. FMNR is a low cost, sustainable land restoration technique used to combat poverty and hunger among poor subsistence farmers by increasing food and timber production, and resilience to climate extremes. FMNR promotes the regrowth of indigenous trees, shrubs and naturally occurring seeds in degraded forest and farmland through farmers and community members undertaking selective pruning and protection to encourage the growth of new shoots. Since 2017 the FMNR technique has been promoted by WV'Z to be used by farmers in Miombo forest ecosystems of Zambia. The development of a carbon program is expected to accelerate the adoption of the technique and provide additional incentives for long term sustainability and permanence.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Global Mangrove Trust Blue Carbon Restoration Project in Indonesia - Sumatra 1
description:
This is a real case VPA-01 under the PoA. This is a transition project from OxCarbon to the Gold Standard for Global Goals. The project under OxCarbon is a community-based conservation and restoration project. The restoration component of the project is being de-registered from OxCarbon and transitioned to GS4GG. 

The CME, GMT, will work with the local NGO, Yayasan Gajah Sumatera (YAGASU) as the VPA Implementer and in association with the local communities. YAGASU, established in 2001, is an Indonesian Foundation having long-term practical experiences on land-based climate actions.  Under this VPA, about 142.82 ha of degraded mangroves will be restored in four villages: Salahaji, Pulau Kampai, Halaban, and Pangkalan Siata in Langkat district, Medan, North Sumatra Province, Indonesia.

Native mangrove species, predominately Rhizophora apiculata, Rhizophora mucronata, Rhizophora stylosa, Ceriops tagal, Bruguiera cylindrica, Bruguiera parviflora and Bruguiera sexangula will be planted on community lands.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Morobe Markham Reforestation Project
description:
The Morobe Markham Reforestation project is a first-of-its-kind reforestation project in the Markham Valley of Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea. It is a partnership between Morobe Markham LLC, the developing partner with extensive experience managing emission reduction projects in Papua New Guinea, PNG Carbon Estate, a team of expert local foresters and plantation experts, and Nature Focus Capital, an experienced funder and manager of carbon emission reduction projects. The project has hired Global Carbon Resources, a US-based carbon project management company, to manage the project, develop the processes and documentation to get the credits issued, sell the carbon credits and distribute the profits according to the agreements with the ILGs within the context of the government regulations. 
The goal of the project is to support community development, climate stability, forest growth, and biodiversity conservation in the Morobe Markham Valley. This project fights for environmental, social, and economic justice, aligning with at least 4 of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals. Additionally, it adheres to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and all local and national labor and land use laws.

name: BaumInvest Flor Saphira Reforestation Project El Capricho & La Catorce
description:
The "BaumInvest Flor Saphira Reforestation Project El Capricho & La Catorce" is the third Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) in Colombia incorporated into the Programme of Activities (PoA): BaumInvest Forest Landscape Restoration Programme (GS11707). The project focuses on ecological restoration of degraded cattle pastures in the Vichada department, Orinoquia region, municipality of Cumaribo, near the villages of El Capricho and La Catorce.

Key objectives include:

i) Climate change mitigation through long-term carbon sequestration via afforestation.
ii) Sustainable development and poverty alleviation by generating long-term employment in remote, economically underserved areas.
iii) Biodiversity conservation by preserving natural habitats and enhancing habitat connectivity.

This initiative integrates ecological, social, and economic dimensions to advance sustainable land use and restoration.

name: Project Oasis VPA-I
description: Arukah is scaling a decentralised cow manure-to-biogas model that links carbon credit revenues with direct incentive payments to farmers for verified biogas use. The initiative involves installing household biodigesters and biogas cookstoves that cut greenhouse gas emissions from animal waste management, reduce reliance on firewood and LPG, and improve indoor air quality. Each unit is paired with a continuous stove monitor (CSM) to track real-time biogas production and consumption, ensuring transparent measurement of verified farmer performance. Verified usage is rewarded through digital payouts, establishing a pioneering model of farmer-level carbon-income distribution. Through this approach, Arukah not only supports climate mitigation but also empowers rural households with cleaner energy access, time savings, and integration into formal digital payment and financing systems, advancing both environmental and socioeconomic outcomes.

name: Clean Cooking in Tanzania: Pay-As-You-Go Smart Metering Solution
description:
The Clean Cooking Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG) Smart Metering Solution aims to reduce the high demand for wood, charcoal, and kerosene traditionally used for cooking in households across targeted areas in Tanzania. Circle Gas achieves this by installing LPG cylinders equipped with smart meters that accurately monitor consumption and enable the PAYG model, making clean cooking accessible to low-income households by removing the barrier of upfront refilling costs.

The primary objective of the Project is to expand LPG access, thus reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and mitigating the adverse impacts of traditional fuel use. Switching from inefficient biomass to clean-burning LPG reduces CO₂ and black carbon emissions, contributing to climate action goals (SDG 13).
By replacing traditional biomass and kerosene with LPG, the program reduces exposure to harmful smoke, benefiting household air quality and health. This shift significantly impacts women and children, who are disproportionately affected by respiratory illnesses linked to Household Air Pollution (HAP), a leading cause of mortality in Africa (SDG 3).
Efficient LPG technology reduces the time women and girls spend on fuel collection, enabling them to pursue income-generating activities and education (SDGs 4 & 5).
The program alleviates the financial burden on low-income households by providing affordable energy alternatives and creating thousands of high-quality jobs (SDG 1).
Affordable, Clean Energy: Expanding access to affordable energy for cooking directly supports sustainable energy goals (SDG 7).
The project creates employment, particularly for youth in sales, service, and overall program management roles (SDG 8).
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Hygiene and Environmental Care for Tanks and Overhead Reservoirs (HECTOR)
description:
The purpose of the Programme of Activities (PoA) entitled “Hygiene and Environmental Care for Tanks and Overhead Reservoirs (HECTOR)”, is to provide safe drinking water to households in rural communities of India. This initiative intends to diminish the reliance on wood fuel and non-renewable biomass for water purification, which would otherwise be necessary in the absence of this project. The project aims to achieve this by deploying automated chlorination units, UV disinfection, and utilizing advanced IoT and AI-ML driven cloud technology for real-time water quality monitoring.  

The geographical boundary and target are households in rural communities with overhead tank reservoirs that have no definitive chlorination or post UV disinfections. This project will provide online access via App to local inhabitants to monitor their water quality online, on their smart phones, and the distributed water will be free of charge to community.

The project is anticipated to yield significant impacts in health, social, environmental, and economic spheres for thousands of individuals in the project area. It will generate employment opportunities in rural areas, particularly in filter manufacturing and distribution, with a focus on gender inclusivity. Furthermore, this project is aligned with various UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to create a comprehensive positive impact.

name: Ayémé solar PV plant
description:
The project involves the commissioning of a photovoltaic power plant which target capacity is 60 MWAC (88 MWp), divided into 2x30 MWAC phases, which will generate around 135 GWh/year. The plant is being built by SOLEN S.A under an agreement between the Gabonese government and the company for the development of a new photovoltaic power plant in the Nkok zone and a 90 kV HV line to evacuate the electricity generated to the Ntoum 2 converter station.
The aim is to reinforce the actions undertaken since the 2000s, aimed at equipping the most remote areas of the country with solar equipment, in order to offset the frequent shortages and reduce the disparities observed with urban areas.
Besides emission reductions impacts and fuel/gas cost savings, economic and social benefits to the local population include around 48 jobs created since construction. The sustainable development impacts of the project activity further comprise:
- Contribution to increased generation capacity in Gabon, in line with the nationally stated goal of a share of renewable energies in the energy mix of 80% by 2030, and by installing new infrastructures that will make it possible to supply an additional 250 MW before 2025.
- Promotion of skills development during construction and operation, The reduction of around 72,210 tCO2e per year and 722,100 tCO2e over the 10 years crediting period

name: GS12771 VPA-3 Sustainable Energy Generation through Biodigester systems in Benin
description:
The proposed VPA involves the installation of 650 biodigester plants with a total capacity of 5,000 m³ across Benin to convert organic waste into biogas, a renewable energy source that replaces fuelwood and fossil fuels commonly used for cooking. The project utilizes locally available biomass resources such as cassava peel waste and animal waste to produce sustainable biogas, offering an integrated solution for clean energy generation and waste management. Cassava, a staple crop in Benin, 
produces large amounts of peel waste that are typically discarded or underutilized; through anaerobic digestion, this waste is converted into methane-rich biogas, reducing methane emissions that would otherwise escape into the atmosphere. The project enhances energy independence, promotes eco friendly waste utilization, and contributes to improved health, sanitation, and agricultural productivity. The biodigester system consists of a fermentation chamber where cassava and animal 
waste decompose in the absence of oxygen, producing biogas for cooking and a nutrient-rich slurry used as organic fertilizer. The project boundary covers the entire biogas value chain from waste collection and digestion to gas use and fertilizer application. Feedstocks include two main categories: animal waste and organic waste such as food waste(cassava peels), or garden residues, etc.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
project_developer: ERDA ILLUMINE LOW CARBON SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED

name: Sustainable Energy Generation through Biodigester systems in Nepal
description: The proposed VPA involves the installation of 6,500 biodigesters across Nepal to convert organic waste into biogas, a renewable energy source that substitutes fuelwood, LPG, charcoal, coal, and kerosene commonly used for domestic cooking. This initiative enhances energy independence by providing locally produced thermal energy while capturing methane a potent greenhouse gas that would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Biogas technology offers multiple co-benefits, including efficient waste management, improved health and sustainable agricultural practices through the use of nutrient-rich digestate as fertilizer. Leveraging Nepal’s substantial livestock population of 116.9 million, including 7.4 million cattle, the project utilizes animal and organic wastes as key feedstocks. The biodigesters function through anaerobic digestion, where bacteria decompose organic materials in anaerobic condition, producing biogas and slurry. The biogas is collected for clean cooking applications, while the slurry is applied as organic fertilizer. The project boundary includes the entire biogas value chain from feedstock collection and digestion to gas utilization and fertilizer application. Two feedstock categories are employed: animal waste and organic waste (such as food waste, paper, or garden waste, etc.). By substituting fossil fuel and reducing methane emissions, the project reduces approximately 59,825 tCO₂e annually.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
project_developer: ERDA ILLUMINE LOW CARBON SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED

name: GS12693 VPA-4 Access to Clean Water in Benin
description:
Access to clean drinking water is still a challenging issue which needs immediate resolution for existence. More than 50% of Beninese living in semi-urban environment do not have access to drinking water. Children suffer from waterborne diseases like diarrhoea and cholera. Girls drop out of school to trek kilometres every day to fetch water. Around 97% of rural households rely on firewood for cooking which also suggests that firewood is the only source used for purifying water for drinking purpose. People are often exposed to suppressed demand in absence of purification technology and 
efforts involved in it. The World Bank has provided International Development Association (IDA) additional financing of $250 million apart from earlier finances to enable Benin to continue its largescale program to provide water access to rural communities. This operation is also in line with the 2021-2026 Government Action Plan and with the World Bank Group’s 2018-2023 Country Partnership Framework for Benin evidencing government focus on provision of clean drinking water to its people. 
The project involves water treatment technology for households, that otherwise boil unsafe drinking water using non-renewable sources and/or depend on the consumption of unsafe water (issue of supressed demand) due to various barrier factors or use energy exhaustive methods to purify water thereby contributing to the emissions by Benin.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
project_developer: ERDA ILLUMINE LOW CARBON SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED

description: The VPA aims to provide energy efficient Improved cookstoves (ICS) to the rural communities in the states of West Bengal and Jharkhand in India who rely on traditional firewood cookstove or 3-stone cookstove to cater clean cooking needs at the same time reduce the greenhouse gas emission resulting from inefficient cooking technology. The project involves the distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to replace the baseline traditional cookstoves in rural households. Here ICS refers to both electric cookstove and Improved firewood cookstove together.  3 billion people rely on wood, coal, charcoal for cooking and heating. The Improved cookstoves can reduce the need of wood by 50%. This results in less harmful greenhouse gas emissions and also considerably reduces the pressure on the local forests and biodiversity. The cookstoves generate less smoke and the chimney limits the exposure to smoke to help fight the problem of indoor air pollution and decrease respiratory diseases.

name: GS12693 VPA-3 Access to Clean Water in Ghana
description:
In Ghana, according to WHO, 7,653 deaths were caused by WASH related illness in 2019, 21 people per day, almost one person every hour dying from preventable WASH-related diseases.  Ghana is striding towards providing 60% of urban families with access to securely managed water services; but, access to these services is substantially lower in rural areas, at just 17%. Indicators of cleanliness also demonstrate this disparity, with 32% of the compared to 9% of people in metropolitan environments, the rural population still urinates outside.
About 25% of all under-5 mortalities are due to diarrhoea. One person out of every ten spend more than 30 minutes to access an improved source of drinking water a burden that is largely tasked on women and children. Another 11 per cent of the population, still drink from surface and other unsafe water sources. the statistics from UNICEF 2023 for The Republic of Ghana reveals 76% of households in Ghana are at risk of drinking water that is contaminated with faecal matter. Moreover, only 4% of households treat water suitably before drinking and 93% of households do not treat water at all which make them vulnerable towards water borne diseases. The current water supply systems are overburdened, and it is further predicted that annual capital expenditures for urban and rural water supply amount to almost US $ 240 million. The Ghana WASH Sector Development Program (GWASHSDP) estimates that $1.7 billion is needed annually for program investment if Ghana should reach the SDG 6. This includes investment requirements for urban water supply estimated at $420 million and rural/community water supply at $350 million annually. 
The project involves water treatment technology for households, that otherwise boil unsafe drinking water using non-renewable sources and/or depend on the consumption of unsafe water (issue of supressed demand) due to various barrier factors or use energy exhaustive methods to purify water thereby contributing to the emissions by Ghana.
